standard_prerequisites.name: Contractibility of the fibers
standard_prerequisites.statement: The hypothesis gives, for every point y of the codomain, a center and a contraction of the fiber of f over y.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure the construction reads off.

standard_prerequisites.name: Half adjoint equivalence data
standard_prerequisites.statement: The data of a half adjoint equivalence are an inverse map, a homotopy from the composite to the identity, and a coherence path relating the two triangle identities.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure that has to be produced.

standard_prerequisites.name: Coherence in the fiber
standard_prerequisites.statement: Giving the coherence datum is the same as giving, for each x, a path in the fiber of f over f(x) between two specified points.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction that makes the construction possible.

core_obligations: From the contraction of the fiber at y define the inverse map by taking the first component of the center (source lines 451-452).
Define the homotopy component by taking the witness that the chosen point lies in the fiber at y (source lines 453-454).
Reduce the remaining coherence datum to a path in the fiber of f over f(x) between two explicitly named points, using the cited coherence lemma (source lines 456-457).

Produce that path by the contraction of the fiber, explicitly as the inverse of one contraction applied to the first point concatenated with the same contraction applied to the second (source lines 457-458).

proof_roadmap.step: Read the inverse map and the homotopy off the contractions of the fibers.
Reduce the coherence datum to a path in a fiber and build it from the contraction.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 447-449 (book Theorem 4.4.3): for every map f, contractibility of its fibers implies that it is a half adjoint equivalence. The statement is an implication between two structures and the proof (source lines 450-458) has to construct each piece of the target structure from the hypothesis: the inverse map is the first component of a center of contraction, the homotopy is the witness that this point lies in the fiber, and the coherence datum, which is where the real work is, is first reduced through the cited lemma to a path inside a fiber and then produced explicitly from the contraction of that fiber as a concatenation of the two contraction paths. The reduction of the coherence to a path in a fiber, and the choice of its two endpoints, are invisible in the statement.
